title: Runtime operational pathways and shard topology
author: Sofia Park
body:
Title: Runtime operational pathways and shard topology

Summary:
This page describes the runtime component dependency map we use to reason about production degradation paths, kernel scheduling interactions, shard placement, and where to attach profiling and benchmarking probes. It is an operational reference for SREs and runtime engineers that ties architecture-level decisions to concrete runbook actions and micro-mitigation steps.

1) Purpose and scope
- Purpose: Provide a single reference linking runtime components, scheduling signals, profiling hooks, and operational procedures.
- Scope: Serving runtime components (router, dispatcher, runtime-core, kernel-manager, kv-cache, shard-manager, telemetry-agent) for hosted, dedicated, and private deployments. Does NOT cover model training or offline data pipelines.

2) High-level diagram (textual)
- Ingress Router -> Request Validator -> Smart Router (policy) -> Shard Manager -> Dispatcher -> Runtime Core (per-shard agent) -> Kernel Manager -> GPU Execution -> KV Cache / Prefetcher -> Telemetry Agent -> Observability pipeline
- Diagram notes: smart routing can bypass shard manager for single-node pinned requests (customer pinned versions). Dispatcher batches requests for the same shard/kernel-selection window.

3) Component responsibilities (short)
- Ingress Router: TLS termination, API auth, rate limiting, token accounting.
- Smart Router: Route by policy (latency-first, cost-first, region, customer tier). Exposes /v1/route-decisions for debugging.
- Shard Manager: Maintains active shard topology, shard-to-GPU mapping, and rebalance operations. Owns topology versioning and exposes /shard-status.
- Dispatcher: Batcher + sequencer. Converts requests into continuous-batch windows and forwards to Runtime Core.
- Runtime Core: Per-shard agent that manages model KV cache, sequence handling, and pre/post-processing hooks.
- Kernel Manager: Chooses kernel variants (fp16, int8, fused-attn) per request-window and triggers kernel hot-swap when safe.
- KV Cache / Prefetcher: Global prefix cache with LRU and sticky-session affinity.
- Telemetry Agent: Streamer for metrics, traces, and profiling frames into observability (OTLP).

4) Shard topology primitives and invariants
- Shard: logical partition of a model replica (weights and persistent kernels).
- Topology version: monotonic integer (v1, v2 ...). All dispatchers and runtime-cores subscribe to topology updates; topology rollout is two-phase (prepare -> commit).
- Invariants: 
  - No two runtime cores should claim the same shard replica write-lock.
  - Topology commit window must be <= 60s to avoid routing ambiguity for SLO-sensitive customers.
  - Kernel hot-swap is permitted only when no active prefix read-locks exist for a shard (see runbook for forcing swap).

5) Kernel scheduling and selection rules (operationally important)
- Priority of selection (highest to lowest): Pinned customer request variant -> Latency SLO mode (lowest-latency kernel set) -> Cost SLO mode (quantized kernels) -> Fallback family (compatible architecture)
- Kernel selection signals: avg_seq_len_1m, kv_hit_ratio, tail_latency_95, gpu_util_60s, queued_requests.
- Default thresholds used by kernel-manager v2.7:
  - tail_latency_95 > 250ms => prefer latency-optimized kernels (fused-attn, fp16).
  - gpu_util_60s > 78% && queued_requests > 16 => consider higher-batch fused kernels or allocate extra shard capacity.
  - kv_hit_ratio < 0.2 => enable prefetch window (30s) or promote hot-prefix caching.

6) Profiling playbook (attach points and quick triage)
- When to profile: sustained tail latency increases > 20% for 5+ minutes or spike in OOMs.
- Attach points: dispatcher, runtime-core (per-shard), kernel-manager, GPU OS proc.
- Quick triage steps (1–5):
  1. Query topology and dispatcher queues: curl -s http://dispatcher:8080/metrics | jq '.queue_lengths'
  2. Snapshot kernel-manager decisions: curl http://kernel-manager:9090/v1/decisions | tee /tmp/km.decisions.json
  3. Collect runtime-core perf counters (30s): /opt/runtime/bin/perf-dump --shard <shard-id> --duration 30s > /tmp/perf.shard
  4. Dump KV cache stats: curl http://kv-cache:7070/stats
  5. Upload traces to observability: /opt/telemetry/bin/submit-frame --reason "incident-triage" --file /tmp/perf.shard
- Pro tips: enable sampling at 10% for request-level traces during high-throughput to avoid observability cost blowouts.

7) Benchmarking suite touchpoints and recommended workloads
- Bench harness components: perf-harness (python), seq-gen (workload generator), harness-orchestrator (k8s job templates).
- Canonical workloads:
  - Small-chat (seq_len=64, avg_toks=16, kv_prefetch_off) — tests latency SLOs.
  - Long-context (seq_len=2048, kv_hit_ratio=0.6) — tests KV cache effectiveness and memory pressure.
  - High-throughput (parallel 256 requests, batch-window=50ms) — tests batching and kernel throughput.
- Representative K8s job snippet (YAML shown as inline code):
```
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: Job
metadata:
  name: perf-small-chat
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: perf-harness
        image: registry.redwood.ai/perf-harness:2025-10
        args: ["--workload", "small-chat", "--duration", "600"]
      restartPolicy: Never
```
- Benchmark measurement taxonomy (always report): P50, P95, P99 end-to-end latency; GPU tokens/sec; average batch size; KV hit ratio; erred requests per 10k.

8) Runtime release notes (summary, useful for operators)
- v3.2.1 (2025-09-18) — patch release
  - Fixed: race during topology commit that could cause duplicate dispatch routes (INC-RED-1479).
  - Added: kernel-manager exposes /v1/decisions with reason codes.
  - Perf: 4–6% throughput improvement on fused-attn kernels for seq <= 128.
- v3.3.0 (2025-11-01) — minor release
  - New: topology prepare/commit now supports staged rollbacks on health-probe mismatch.
  - New: telemetry agent supports compressed OTLP frames reducing observability egress by ~30%.
  - Breaking change: default dispatcher.batch-window reduced from 75ms to 50ms; see rollout steps below.

9) Rollout checklist for dispatcher.batch-window change (required for any env)
1. Create a canary pool with new config (10% of traffic).
2. Run correctness smoke: perf-small-chat, 30m, check p95 delta < 10% and error delta < 0.01%.
3. Monitor GPU util and queued_requests for 1 hour.
4. If regressions observed, revert config via topology rollback: curl -X POST http://shard-manager:8080/v1/topology/rollback -d '{"version":<old>}'
5. Promote to 50% then 100% following same checks.

10) Known issues (operationally actionable)
- KNOWN-2024-031: Kernel hot-swap can stall when a long-running completion (seq > 3k) holds a read-lock longer than the swap timeout (default 120s). Mitigation: increase swap_timeout to 300s for affected model families or schedule swap during low-traffic windows. Owner: runtime-core team.
- KNOWN-2025-008: Under high small-request QPS with low avg_seq_len (<12) and aggressive batch-window (<=25ms) we observe increased context-switch overhead on dispatcher pods leading to higher p95. Mitigation: raise batch-window to 50ms for those workloads or pin to latency-optimized kernels. Owner: dispatcher team.
- KNOWN-2025-021: Rare KV cache eviction thrashing for long-context workloads when two large prefixes are near-simultaneously promoted. Mitigation: enable sticky-prefix mode for the affected customer or increase cache-size-gb by 10%. Owner: cache team.

11) Runbooks (short form)
- Runbook: Degraded tail latency (p95 > SLO)
  1. Confirm: check p95 on /dashboards/runtime/p95-live and SLO config for route.
  2. Check dispatcher queues; if queue_length > 100, scale dispatcher replicas (kubectl scale deploy/dispatcher --replicas=N+2).
  3. Check kernel-manager decision stream for sudden kernel downgrades. If a downgrade to quantized variants is active, roll back using /kernel-manager/v1/force-variant?variant=latency_opt.
  4. If GPU util > 90% and queue persists, scale shard capacity or enable burst-pool routing.
  5. Collect full profiling snapshot (see section 6) and attach to incident.
- Runbook: Stuck topology commit
  1. Verify logs on shard-manager for prepare/commit errors.
  2. If transaction lock present, escalate to runtime-core oncall and run /opt/runtime/bin/topo-unlock --version <version>.
  3. Re-run health probes and re-commit.

12) Operational scripts and CLI examples (copyable)
- Dump active topology: curl -s http://shard-manager:8080/v1/topology | jq . > /tmp/topo.json - Force kernel variant: curl -X POST http://kernel-manager:9090/v1/force-variant -d '{"shard":"shard-42","variant":"fp16-fused"}'
- KV cache stats: curl http://kv-cache:7070/stats | jq '.cache_entries|length, .hit_ratio'

13) Ownership, escalation, and contact matrix
- runtime-core: owner-runtime-core@redwood.ai (oncall: @runtime-core-oncall)
- dispatcher: owner-dispatcher@redwood.ai (oncall: @dispatcher-oncall)
- kernel-manager: owner-kernel@redwood.ai (oncall: @kernel-oncall)
- cache: owner-kv@redwood.ai (oncall: @kv-oncall)
- SRE escalation: sre-escalation@redwood.ai

14) How this ties to team wiki and deeper pages
- This page is the operational glue. For design rationales see team wiki: /confluence/eng-serving-runtime/team-wiki/runtime-design-notes-2024. For deep dives on profiling, see profiling-playbook/runtime-profiling-playbook-guidelines-2025. Kernel scheduler spec lives at kernel-and-scheduling/priority-driven-kernel-scheduler-spec-2026. Benchmark job templates and historical runs are in benchmarking-and-perf-suite/perf-archive-2025.

15) Appendix: metric thresholds and SLOs (table rendered inline)
- SLOs (default route):
  - p95 latency <= 220ms for small-chat workloads
  - p99 latency <= 420ms for small-chat workloads
  - availability >= 99.95% (monthly)
- Metric thresholds:
  - dispatcher.queue_length (warning) > 40; (critical) > 120
  - gpu_util_60s (warning) > 78%; (critical) > 92%
  - kv_hit_ratio (warning) < 0.35; (critical) < 0.15
